repo.name: OpenSatFinder
repo.description: This is a repository of apps to be used with F-Droid. Applications in this repository are either official binaries built by the original application developers, or are binaries built from source by the admin of f-droid.org using the tools on https://gitlab.com/fdroid.

application.name: OpenSatFinder
application.summary: Aim a satellite dish at a geostationary satellite with your phone.
application.desc:
OpenSatFinder turns your phone into the instrument you use to aim a satellite dish.
Choose a satellite from the built-in catalogue of geostationary satellites. The compass shows where the phone is pointing and where the satellite sits; the arc underneath shows the elevation, the angle above the horizon, for the phone and for the satellite. Turn and lift until the screen goes green: that is within two degrees of where the dish has to look. Two tones, one for the bearing and one for the elevation, let you aim without watching the screen.
• Compass corrected for magnetic declination, from your position • Elevation gauge: the phone's tilt against the satellite's own elevation • Every geostationary satellite CelesTrak lists, searchable, ordered by elevation • Favourites, and a setting that hides the satellites below the horizon • Audible cues in five volume steps • Eight languages: Catalan, English, Basque, French, Galician, German, Portuguese, Spanish
Privacy: the position never leaves the phone. The app has no network permission at all: no account, no tracking, no advertising and nothing to buy.
OpenSatFinder is free software, licensed under the GNU GPL v3 or later. The source is at https://github.com/Treboada/OpenSatFinder
